preamble: The Middle Chinese voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] of the 常/禪 initial (Baxter dzy-, Zhengzhang /dʑ/) became the aspirated retroflex affricate [ʈʂʰ] in many level-tone (平) syllables of Mandarin, the regular Mandarin treatment of voiced obstruents in the level tone. This follows the modern reconstruction of Pulleyblank, Baxter and Zhengzhang Shangfang, in which 禪 is the affricate [dʑ] and 船 the fricative [ʑ]; the Song rime tables, followed by Karlgren, have the two values swapped. In the oblique tones (rising, departing, entering) dzy- went to the fricative [ʂ] instead (受 shòu, 十 shí; see j_palatal_to_sh_retroflex), and the level-tone outcome is not uniform: 時 dzyi and 誰 dzywij have Mandarin shí and shuí with [ʂ].
sources: Baxter, William H. (1992). A Handbook of Old Chinese Phonology. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110857085
